chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
chunks.marginal_note: Right of individuals to be dealt with in accordance with law
chunks.text: Every citizen, and every other person for the time being within Pakistan, has the inalienable right to enjoy the protection of law and to be treated in accordance with law. In particular, no action detrimental to life, liberty, body, reputation or property may be taken except in accordance with law.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
chunks.marginal_note: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of fundamental rights to be void
chunks.text: Any law, custom or usage having the force of law that is inconsistent with the fundamental rights conferred by this Chapter is void to the extent of the inconsistency. The State may not make any law that takes away or abridges those rights.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
chunks.text: No person may be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
chunks.marginal_note: Safeguards as to arrest and detention
chunks.text: A person who is arrested must be informed of the grounds of arrest as soon as may be, and may not be denied the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice. An arrested person must be produced before a magistrate within twenty-four hours of arrest, excluding travel time, and may not be detained beyond that period without the magistrate's authority.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
chunks.text: For the determination of civil rights and obligations, or in any criminal charge against a person, that person is entitled to a fair trial and due process. This article was inserted by the Eighteenth Amendment in 2010.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
chunks.text: The dignity of man and, subject to law, the privacy of the home are inviolable. No person may be subjected to torture for the purpose of extracting evidence.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
chunks.text: Every citizen has the right to freedom of speech and expression, and there is freedom of the press, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of the glory of Islam, the integrity, security or defence of Pakistan, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, or in relation to contempt of court, or incitement to an offence.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
chunks.text: Every citizen has the right to have access to information in all matters of public importance, subject to regulation and reasonable restrictions imposed by law. This article was inserted by the Eighteenth Amendment in 2010.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part II, Chapter 1: Fundamental Rights
chunks.text: All citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection of law. There is to be no discrimination on the basis of sex alone. Nothing in this article prevents the State from making special provision for the protection of women and children.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part VII, Chapter 2: The Supreme Court
chunks.marginal_note: Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
chunks.text: The Supreme Court has original jurisdiction in disputes between governments. Under clause (3), where the Court considers that a question of public importance arises with reference to the enforcement of any of the fundamental rights, it may make an order of the nature mentioned in Article 199.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part VII, Chapter 2: The Supreme Court
chunks.marginal_note: Decisions of Supreme Court binding on other courts
chunks.text: Any decision of the Supreme Court, to the extent that it decides a question of law or is based upon or enunciates a principle of law, is binding on all other courts in Pakistan.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part VII, Chapter 3: The High Courts
chunks.text: A High Court may, if satisfied that no other adequate remedy is provided by law, issue directions to a person performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Federation, a Province or a local authority. This is the constitutional writ jurisdiction, covering orders in the nature of mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, habeas corpus and quo warranto.

chunks.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.chapter: Part VII, Chapter 3: The High Courts
chunks.marginal_note: Decisions of High Court binding on subordinate courts
chunks.text: Subject to Article 189, any decision of a High Court, to the extent that it decides a question of law or is based upon or enunciates a principle of law, is binding on all courts subordinate to it.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XVI: Offences Affecting the Human Body
chunks.text: Punishment for intentional murder. A person guilty of qatl-i-amd is liable to punishment under clause (a) as qisas, under clause (b) with death or imprisonment for life as ta'zir having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case if the proof in clause (a) is not available, or under clause (c) with imprisonment of either description for up to twenty-five years where the offence has not been proved under clause (a) or (b).

chunks.chapter: Chapter XVI: Offences Affecting the Human Body
chunks.marginal_note: Punishment for qatl-i-khata by rash or negligent driving
chunks.text: Whoever commits qatl-i-khata by rash or negligent driving is liable to diyat and may also be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years. Note that this is a distinct offence from Section 302 and the two are commonly confused because of the similar numbers.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XVI: Offences Affecting the Human Body
chunks.text: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that, if that act caused death, the person would be guilty of qatl-i-amd, is punishable with imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years, and is also liable to fine. Where hurt is caused, the offender is additionally liable to the punishment provided for that hurt.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XVII: Offences Against Property
chunks.text: Whoever commits theft is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XVII: Offences Against Property
chunks.text: Whoever commits robbery is punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and is also liable to fine. Where the robbery is committed on a highway between sunset and sunrise, the term of imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XVII: Offences Against Property
chunks.text: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe it to be stolen property, is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XVII: Offences Against Property
chunks.marginal_note: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
chunks.text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy any valuable security, is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and is also liable to fine.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XVIII: Offences Relating to Documents
chunks.text: Whoever dishonestly issues a cheque towards repayment of a loan or fulfilment of an obligation which is dishonoured on presentation is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both, unless the person can establish that reasonable arrangements had been made with the bank for payment.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XXII: Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
chunks.text: Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Where the threat is to cause death or grievous hurt, or to destroy property by fire, the punishment may extend to seven years.

chunks.chapter: Chapter V: Arrest, Escape and Retaking
chunks.marginal_note: When police may arrest without warrant
chunks.text: A police officer may arrest without an order from a magistrate and without a warrant any person who has been concerned in a cognizable offence, or against whom a reasonable complaint has been made or credible information received or reasonable suspicion exists of such involvement, among other enumerated categories.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XIV: Information to the Police and their Powers to Investigate
chunks.text: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence given orally to an officer in charge of a police station must be reduced to writing, read over to the informant, and signed by that person. The substance is to be entered in a book kept for that purpose. This is the provision under which a First Information Report is registered.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XIV: Information to the Police and their Powers to Investigate
chunks.text: A police officer making an investigation may examine orally any person supposed to be acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case. Such a person is bound to answer all questions other than those which would expose them to a criminal charge, penalty or forfeiture.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XIV: Information to the Police and their Powers to Investigate
chunks.marginal_note: Report of police officer on completion of investigation
chunks.text: On completion of the investigation, the officer in charge of the police station must forward a report to the magistrate empowered to take cognizance of the offence, setting out the parties, the nature of the information, the witnesses, whether an offence appears to have been committed and by whom, and whether the accused has been arrested or released on bond. This report is commonly called the challan.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XX: Trial of Cases by Magistrates
chunks.marginal_note: Power of magistrate to acquit accused at any stage
chunks.text: A magistrate may, at any stage of the case after hearing the prosecutor and the accused and for reasons to be recorded, acquit the accused if the magistrate considers that the charge is groundless or that there is no probability of the accused being convicted of any offence.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XXIIA: Trial before Court of Session
chunks.marginal_note: Power of court to acquit accused at any stage
chunks.text: Notwithstanding anything in the Code, if at any stage of the case the court considers that there is no probability of the accused being convicted of any offence, it may acquit the accused at any stage after hearing the prosecutor and the accused, for reasons to be recorded. This is the Sessions Court counterpart of Section 249-A.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XXXIX: Bail
chunks.marginal_note: When bail may be taken in cases of non-bailable offence
chunks.text: A person accused of a non-bailable offence may be released on bail, but not where there appear reasonable grounds for believing that the person is guilty of an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life or imprisonment for ten years. Exceptions apply, including where the accused is under sixteen years of age, a woman, or sick or infirm. Bail may also be granted on the ground of statutory delay in the conclusion of trial.

chunks.chapter: Chapter XXXIX: Bail
chunks.marginal_note: Power to direct admission to bail or reduction of bail
chunks.text: The High Court or Court of Session may direct that any person be admitted to bail, or that the bail required by a police officer or magistrate be reduced. This provision is the basis on which pre-arrest bail is sought.
